rationale: Block 3 covers clinical presentation of anxiety disorders including GAD duration criteria — tests application of the ≥6 months criterion to a new case.
Block 6 covers excluding medical mimics before diagnosing anxiety — directly tests whether learners understand this primary care diagnostic priority.
Block 8 covers management principles — tests first-line pharmacotherapy choice, a common NEET/clinical exam and practical prescribing question in primary care.
Block 3 covers the clinical presentation and diagnostic spectrum (ASD vs PTSD vs Adjustment Disorder) — tests application of the timeline-first differential in a case vignette.
Block 6 directly covers the ASD/PTSD/Adjustment Disorder differential using the timeline. Tests the key distinguishing principle between ASD and PTSD durations.
Block 8 covers management and referral criteria — tests the decision to refer vs manage at primary care, the most clinically important skill in PS8.1.
